assessment.nobel_worthiness: Legal origins and investor protection created a new empirical research program in finance, law and development. It linked legal institutions to financial development and corporate governance through cross-country measurement. The work has had a large, durable impact on research and on policy debates about institutions and finance.
assessment.attribution: The core 'Law and Finance' and 'Legal Determinants of External Finance' papers were written by La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny. Vishny's main role was in the 1997-98 papers, so the proposal credits the three authors who carried the program forward. Shleifer also has wider contributions beyond this program.
assessment.maturity: The foundational papers date from 1997-2008, so the work has had decades to be tested, extended and criticised. The 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity covered adjacent but distinct ground.
uncertainties: The causal interpretation of legal-origin effects has been challenged, and some measures have been revised (e.g. the anti-director index). Replicability and robustness of the cross-country regressions are a concern.
Overlap with the 2024 institutions prize may weigh on the timing.
Excluding Vishny is a judgment call about the credit split.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, staggered pricing and wage setting, and the policy-rule framework form the basis of how modern central banks model and conduct monetary policy. The work has high practical and theoretical influence.
assessment.attribution: Calvo (1983) gave the workhorse pricing model, Taylor gave staggered contracts and the Taylor rule, and Woodford gave the microfounded policy framework. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets also made major contributions, so a three-person cap forces hard choices about credit.
assessment.maturity: The core ideas date from the 1980s to the early 2000s and have been tested and refined over decades. Some of the debate has moved on to heterogeneous-agent models.
uncertainties: Many deserving contributors compete for at most three places, so attribution is contested.
Post-2008 and post-2021 inflation episodes raise questions about the empirical performance of the framework.
The committee has recently recognised other macro work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection changed how trade is analysed. Gains from trade now operate through reallocation across firms, and the framework is the basis of a large empirical literature using firm-level data. The framework is widely used for policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution, and Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple (2004) extended it to exporting versus FDI. Redding is credited for later quantitative work. Other important contributors, such as Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum, are outside this credited set.
assessment.maturity: The work is more than twenty years old and heavily used. Trade has not been recognised since 2008, so the timing is plausible.
uncertainties: Others, including Bernard and Jensen on empirical firm facts, could claim part of the credit.
Overlap with the quantitative trade candidate (B002) and the political-economy trade candidate (B013).
Some predictions depend on functional-form assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run series on top incomes and wealth, built from tax records, reshaped both research and public debate on inequality. The work created a data infrastructure that other researchers and agencies now use.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez started the top-income series, and Zucman extended them to wealth and offshore wealth. Atkinson, who is deceased, was an important contributor. Zucman's work is younger, and the proposal leaves him out because it focuses on the foundational contribution.
assessment.maturity: The foundational work dates from 2003, with more than twenty years of use. Parts of the wealth and offshore work are more recent and still debated.
uncertainties: The measurement methods and the interpretation of the r>g argument are contested, with disputes about data construction and the statistical treatment of top shares.
It is a judgment call whether data and measurement fit the prize better than the underlying theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine learning for causal inference, including double/debiased machine learning, causal forests and heterogeneous treatment-effect estimation, gave applied researchers rigorous tools for high-dimensional settings. The methods are used across the social sciences and in industry. They are relevant to credible-inference practice because they come with valid inference and honest estimation.
assessment.attribution: Chernozhukov and co-authors developed double machine learning, while Athey and Wager developed causal forests and related work. Imbens, Hansen and others are close contributors, so credit is distributed. The proposal names Athey and Chernozhukov as the most prominent figures, but Wager's role is arguably equal for the forest methods.
assessment.maturity: Most of the key work dates from 2016-2018, which is less than a decade ago. The methods are rapidly adopted but their long-run influence is still being established.
uncertainties: The work is relatively recent, and the committee may prefer to wait.
Credit is spread across many authors.
Practical gains over simpler methods can vary by application.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Models of present bias and reference dependence brought psychologically realistic preferences into mainstream economic theory. They have been applied to savings, consumption, and policy design for health and retirement. The impact extends well beyond the field.
assessment.attribution: Laibson (quasi-hyperbolic discounting), Rabin (reference dependence and fairness), O'Donoghue (naive vs sophisticated present bias), Koszegi (reference-dependent preferences) and Loewenstein (psychological foundations) all contributed. Attribution is diffuse. The earlier prizes to Kahneman (2002) and Thaler (2017) covered related ground.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from the 1990s-2000s and is well established, with many field and lab tests.
uncertainties: Overlap with the Kahneman and Thaler prizes may reduce the incremental case.
Evidence on the empirical magnitude of present bias and loss aversion is mixed, with replication concerns in some behavioural findings, which I weigh as a caution.
The credit split among five names is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural estimation of demand with differentiated products and endogenous prices (BLP) became the standard tool in industrial organisation and antitrust. The dynamic industry models of Ericson-Pakes extended the program. The impact on empirical practice and merger analysis is high.
assessment.attribution: The BLP papers (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes 1995 and Berry 1994) are clearly attributable, and Pakes also led the dynamic-games work. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are credited for related contributions that are outside this proposal.
assessment.maturity: The work is thirty years old with extensive validation and use in practice.
uncertainties: The committee may judge the contribution as more methodological than conceptual.
Credit for the empirical IO program could be drawn differently, including to Bresnahan.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Persson and Tabellini built the modern theoretical and empirical framework linking electoral rules, constitutions and fiscal outcomes. It is a coherent research program with wide influence, including on policy-relevant questions about political institutions.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the central figures of the program, and Besley has important parallel work on state capacity. Excluding Besley is a judgment call. Possible overlap with the 2024 institutions laureates affects relative standing.
assessment.maturity: The program is more than twenty years old and well assessed, with a major synthesis book (2000) and a large literature that followed.
uncertainties: The 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity may reduce the appetite for another award in a nearby area.
Some of the empirical cross-country results rely on observational variation, with identification concerns.
The credit to Besley versus Persson and Tabellini is uncertain.
